mara: quick flag - after the overnight surge in us-west2 we still see high pcie stall correlation even for tenants moved to dedicated carveouts. hypothesis: carveouts landed on same PCIe root complex as noisy hosts. proposing we add a lightweight PCIe-root dimension and a carveout preflight to avoid co-root placements.

ben: agreed. we only have rack/slot metadata today. discovery job + inventory tag sounds right. canary on a single rack first.

ryan: sketch: discovery-run -> inventoryctl push pcie_root_id per GPU -> scheduler respects `spread_pcie_root=true` for carveouts. Also add `fleetctl carveout --check-pcie-root` preflight to fail noisy placements.

mara: sample commands (canary):
```
ansible-playbook playbooks/discover_pcie_root.yml --limit=rack33-host[01..03]
inventoryctl tag push --source=pcie-discover-canary --ttl=7d --hosts=rack33-host[01..03]
schedulerctl feature-flag set spread_pcie_root=true --scope=carveouts
fleetctl carveout create --tenant=t-video --cards=1 --region=us-west2 --check-pcie-root
```

ben: metrics to watch: host.pcie_stalls p95, tenant.preempt_count, scheduler.placement_latency.p50. Alert if pcie_stalls doesn't drop by >10% after canary or if placement_latency > 250ms.

infra-bot: CHANGE scheduled: CHANGE-7265 by mara - discovery canary 2026-04-10T23:00:00Z. Runbook: https://wiki.redwood.internal/runbooks/pcie-root-playbook.

ryan: also add a simple `lspci` probe in the carveout post-check: `fleetctl carveout verify --probe=lspci-root` that runs once and reports root paths. helps catch odd cabling.

mara: i'll run the canary tonight and post results here. ben take pager for first 2h.
